eventMetadata.context_description: The match between Everton FC and Manchester United FC concluded in a 2-2 draw at Hill Dickinson Stadium, locking in the outcome as the sole resolution for this market. Everton twice rallied from deficits, with Tyrique George equalizing in the 83rd minute before debutant Ainsley Maitland-Niles scored a stoppage-time winner from distance. Manchester United had led through Bryan Mbeumo's early second-half strike and Benjamin Sesko's 88th-minute header. Official Premier League confirmation of the final score drives the complete market consensus, with no further variables such as protests or appeals altering the result.

title: Counter-Strike: Spirit vs MOUZ (BO5) - BLAST Open Porto Playoffs
description:
This market refers to the Counter-Strike Grand final match between Spirit and MOUZ in the BLAST Open Porto Playoffs, initially scheduled for September 6, 2026 at 10:00 AM ET.

This market will resolve to "Spirit" if Spirit win the match against MOUZ.

This market will resolve to "MOUZ" if MOUZ win the match against Spirit.

If the match is canceled (not played at all) or ends in a tie, this market will resolve to 50-50.

If the match is postponed, it must be rescheduled to a start time on or before September 20, 2026 at 11:59 PM ET (14 calendar days after the originally scheduled start of September 6, 2026 at 10:00 AM ET). If, by that deadline, the most recently announced rescheduled start time is on or before the deadline, this market resolves based on the result of the match as played. Otherwise, this market resolves 50-50, regardless of whether the match is subsequently played.

If the match begins but is not completed, and one team wins due to the opponent's forfeiture, disqualification, or walkover, this market will resolve to the team who wins. 

If the match ends in a forfeit, disqualification, or walkover (team withdraws before the start and the other wins automatically), this market will resolve to 50-50. 

The resolution source for this market will be official information from https://hltv.org. However, if https://hltv.org has not published final results within 2 hours after the event’s conclusion, a consensus of credible reporting may be used instead including video evidence.

In cases where a team’s listed name includes minor discrepancies from the resolution source, this market will resolve based on the underlying real-world match rather than exact name matching. Recognizable abbreviations, alternate or erroneous spellings, sponsor tags, affiliate or academy designations, regional identifiers, and minor formatting differences will be treated as referring to the same team, provided the intended team can be clearly and uniquely identified within the relevant competition. If a listed team name has no reasonable connection to any participating team, or if it matches or could reasonably refer to another team in the same competition such that the intended team cannot be unambiguously determined, this market will resolve 50-50.

eventMetadata.context_description: Spirit enters the BLAST Open Porto 2026 grand final as the clear favorite, holding the world #1 ranking and a 10-match win streak that includes dominant group-stage and semifinal sweeps over G2, FURIA, and Falcons. Their core of donk, sh1ro, and zont1x has posted elite ratings across recent events, while map advantages on Ancient and strong historical edges bolster their position. MOUZ, ranked #5 and fresh off a 2-0 semifinal win over Vitality, carries momentum from their 3-1 BO5 victory over Spirit in the August BLAST Bounty final, with solid showings on Nuke and Dust2. Traders price Spirit near 65% implied probability on the back of superior recent consistency and head-to-head volume, though MOUZ’s ability to exploit specific map picks and force deep series keeps the underdog outcome viable in a high-stakes BO5.

eventMetadata.context_description: Ninjas in Pyjamas entered the LPL Split 3 lower-bracket quarterfinals riding strong momentum after sweeping JD Gaming 3-0 and remaining undefeated in recent best-of-five series during the third split. LGD Gaming advanced through resilient playoff performances, including a 3-2 comeback over Top Esports, though they carried a more inconsistent regular-season record. The matchup featured contrasting rosters, with NIP relying on Hoya, Care, Photic, Guwon, and Fengyue, while LGD fielded Crisp, Shaoye, Tangyuan, Burdol, and Heng. Both sides faced elimination, with the winner advancing toward a potential bubble match for international qualification, and historical head-to-head data plus recent form shaped trader assessments of the evenly matched BO5.
